The Secure Juvenile Services shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work entitled, "Juvenile Secure SOW March 2025�. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. title: Y--NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice: NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant PURPOSE: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Upper Colorado Basin Region, Four Corners Construction Office (FCCO), is issuing this pre-solicitation notice for a contemplated construction project titled: Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant. This requirement is being procured in accordance with Part 14 of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) with a set-aside for small businesses. The Bureau of Reclamation intends to issue a competitive solicitation for this requirement. Based on market research it was determined that there were a sufficient number of qualified small businesses with sufficient bonding capacity to perform as the prime contractor on this project, and as such, it is anticipated to be set-aside for small businesses. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) is a major infrastructure project that once constructed, will convey a reliable municipal and industrial water supply from the San Juan River to the eastern section of the Navajo Nation, southwestern portion of the Jicarilla Apache Nation, and the city of Gallup, New Mexico via approximately 280 miles of pipeline, several pumping plants, and two water treatment plants. The principal components of work for the Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Pre-engineered concrete booster pump station, concrete foundation pad, pipe encasement, yard pipe, fencing, electrical equipment, gravel surfacing, and pipe connections. 2. Installation of secondary regulation tank at Regulation Tank No. 3 site, foundation, electrical equipment, yard pipe, and pipe connections. 3. Erosion and scour restoration/prevention: a. Includes a retaining wall, swale, runoff channel, and site regrading. 4. Reinstallation of gravel surfacing at Regulation Tank No. 3 site. 5. Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) equipment and radio communications system. LOCATION OF THE WORK: The NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant is located approximately 26 miles South of Bloomfield, NM off County Road 7575 near U.S. Highway 550, at the base of Huerfano Mesa in San Juan County, New Mexico. NAICS AND SIZE STANDARD: The NAICS code for this project is 237110 (Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction) with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. COMPETITION: Solicitation 140R4026B0003 is anticipated to be conducted as a small business set-aside. The project specifications and project location will be defined in the solicitation document. The solicitation will require a bid guarantee of at least 20% of the bid price. The Contract will require payment and performance bonds for 100% of the contract price. Offerors must have sufficient bonding capacity. DISCLOSURE OF THE MAGNITUDE OF THE CONSTRUCTION PROJECT: The magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION RELEASE DATE: All responsible sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A free, electronic copy of the solicitation will be available on APPROXIMATELY November 2, 2026, at https://www.sam.gov/. Simply type in solicitation number "140R4026B0003" in the Keyword / Solicitation # field. A draft solicitation for comment has been attached to this announcement. The purpose of the draft solicitation is for comments only. When comments are received and incorporated, the solicitation will be posted requesting the submission of proposals. This project will follow a best-value procurement process under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 14. Questions and comments must be submitted in writing by e-mail to Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov and Tyler Spencer, at tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM, www.sam.gov): The System for Award Management (SAM) is a recently implemented Federal Government owned-and-operated FREE web site that consolidates the capabilities in Central Contractor Registration (CCR)/Federal Register (FedReg), Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). Offerors must be successfully registered in SAM in order to be considered for a government contract award. If you had an active record in CCR, you have an active record in SAM. SITE VISIT: The Government intends to conduct a site visit for highly interested vendors AROUND November 12, 2026. Information regarding the site visit will be in Section L of the solicitation once released. POINT-OF-CONTACT FOR QUESTIONS: The Contract Specialist for this solicitation is Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov. The Contracting Officer for this solicitation is Tyler Spencer, tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. Any communication regarding this procurement must be made in writing and forwarded via email and must identify the solicitation number, company name, address, email address, phone number including area code, and point of contact. Emails shall be addressed to the Contract Specialist and cc the Contracting Officer. NOTE: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (SOLICITATION), AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), NOR IS IT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). It is not to be construed as a commitment by the requesting party to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals, bids, or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this Notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this Notice. This FedBizOps Notice is strictly for compliance with FAR Subpart 5.2. As a result of this Notice, the Government may issue a competitive solicitation; however, should such requirements materialize, no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to the Notice (e.g. use of such information as either part of its evaluation process or in developing specifications for any subsequent requirement). THE CURRENT SOLICITATION NUMBER 140R4026B0003 (A FISCAL YEAR 2026 SOLICITATION NUMBER) WILL BE UPDATED AFTER OCTOBER 10, 2026, TO A FISCAL YEAR 2027 SOLICITATION NUMBER. SOLICITATION IS EXPECTED TO BE ISSUED IN EARLY NOVEMBER 2026. THIS IS A RESULT OF GOVERNMENT SYSTEM LIMITATIONS. AN ADDENDUM WILL BE ISSUED TO THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE WITH THE NEW SOLICITATION NUMBER.

THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. The purpose of this synopsis is to notify potential Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), in accordance with the requirements of Public Law 109-461 of this requirement. The Gulf Coast Veterans Health Care System has a requirement to Install Catwalks and Safety Railings for Aboveground Fuel Tank; project # 520-27-102, located at Biloxi, MS. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, expertise, administration, supervision transportation and anything else necessary to perform all work as described in project Scope of Work, Drawings, and Specifications. The applicable North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) primary code is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Construction Cost Range for this project (Magnitude of Construction) is between $250,000 and $500,000. Interested offerors are asked to please first read over the RFP and all its associated attachments/documents in their entirety prior to forwarding any questions/Requests for Information (RFI s) to the Contracting Officer. A cut-off time/date for receipt of questions will be established and listed in the RFP as well as a time/date for the scheduled Site Visit. Only one Site Visit will be conducted and no requests for additional Site Visits or make-up Site Visits will be granted. Anticipated contract will be awarded using FAR 15.101-1, Tradeoff Process. This project will require a Bid Bond. A Site-Visit is planned and the information to support this site visit will be provided with actual solicitation. In accordance with VAAR 819.7003 Eligibility, at the time of submission of a proposal, the offeror must represent to the Contracting Officer that it is a SDVOSB concern, that it is a small business concern under the NAICS Code assigned to the acquisition, and that it is certified for eligibility in the� SBA certification database at� https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/� (see 13 CFR 128). title: Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office within the USACE Philadelphia (NAP) District area of responsibility in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is responsible for scheduling work in accordance with the requirements of task order issued and during regular business hours when scheduling on site work. The site conducts regular business from 7:00am to 3:00pm, Monday through Friday, except for federal holidays. All work is to be performed during these regular business hours. Any hours to be worked outside of the regular business hours shall be coordinated with the COR. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform preventative maintenance and repair of heavy equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. The Fort Mifflin Project Office is responsible for the construction of the district�s disposal areas located along the Delaware River. Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. It is important that dredging and proper disposal activities of dredge materials is accomplished because it directly effects commerce and the safety of vessels transporting commodities and other resources to the ports. See attachment labeled "W912BU26QA024_FMPO Combined Solicitation Synopsis.pdf" with the requirements of this RFQ and other attachments required for informational and submission purposes.

description: SOLICITATION SPE603-26-R-0543 Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy - FESAB is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO) Fuel Storage, Operations, and Distribution services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC) 29 Palms, CA. The Contractor will be responsible for the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory control and accounting, security, safety, and environmental protection of the Marine Corps GOCO and COCO fuel facilities. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The contractor must receive, maintain, store, sample and test, internal transfer, and issue petroleum products. The contractor must be responsible for all fuel-servicing operations and safeguarding facilities, equipment, and fuel products under its control during normal and adverse conditions. The contractor must track aviation fuels inventories and order products as needed to meet DLA Energy Accounting Policies and maintain levels to ensure uninterrupted service. This procurement is 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding a firm fixed-price contract. The Period of Performance (PoP) will be from March 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (COCO PoP 3.5-yearbase), September 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (GOCO PoP 3-year base), four, five-year option periods from September 15, 2031 � September 14, 2036 (1st Option); September 15,2036 � September 14, 2041 (2nd Option); September 15, 2041 � September 14, 2046 (3rdOption); September 15, 2046 � September 14, 2051 (4th Option), one, 4.5-year option period from September 15, 2051 - March 14, 2056 (5th Option); and an option to extend the contract not to exceed six (6) months from March 15, 2056 through September 14, 2056. This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources in accordance with FAR 6.206, Set-Asides for service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns eligible under the SDVOSB Program and FAR 19.14, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Program. title: Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: 1. AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. 2. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bid, a solicitation, or an indication the US Air Force (AF) or AFLCMC/WIW will contract for the items contained in the sources sought. AFLCMC/WIW will not pay respondents for information provided in response to the sources sought. 3. The Government is requesting information from vendors of all business sizes including socioeconomic programs such as 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) that are interested in performing this requirement. The Government requests interested parties submit a brief description of their company�s business size (i.e., annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, or SDVOSB, Women Owned Small Business, or small business), and any anticipated teaming arrangements. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision. 4. Interested parties should submit a capabilities package, with a cover letter, that is brief and concise yet clearly demonstrates ability to meet the stated requirements with sufficiently qualified personnel. Provide qualification information (type and duration of employee experience relevant to the requirements) and the level of involvement (prime or sub-contractor) and time periods for work on similar projects. The capabilities package should clearly present evidence that the interested party is fully capable of providing the required services and as such may contain any information that the interested party feels relevant. 5. Responses should be submitted electronically, and must be no more than ten single-spaced pages, using 12-point, Times New Roman font, and minimum one-inch margins, in Microsoft Word format. Responses that only provide a company website will not be considered. 6. Responses to the sources sought are requested by 3PM, CDT, 12 October 2026. All responses shall be unclassified and reviewed to ensure consideration. All responses, correspondence, and/or questions related to this matter should be e-mailed to: E-mail: phaedra.prather@us.af.mil Phone: (405) 739-4340 Attachments: DAR 400 Follow On SOW_Sep 2026 DAR Follow-On draft CDRL_DID Package 2026

title: Europe South District Playground Inspection, Maintenance, and Repair
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is one of only two federally operated school systems in the United States. DoWEA plans, directs, coordinates, and manages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA operates approximately 165 brick-and-mortar schools across eight districts located in seven U.S. states, eleven foreign countries, Guam, and Puerto Rico, serving more than 72,000 students worldwide. DoWEA Europe consists of multiple districts encompassing schools, District Superintendent Offices (DSOs), and Student Transportation Offices (STOs) supporting children of active-duty military members and eligible civilian employees. The Contractor shall provide full-service, performance-based playground inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, emergency response, cleaning services for DoWEA facilities located in Europe South Region. For the purposes of this PWS, playgrounds include all playground systems and associated features, whether standalone or co-located, including but not limited to: Playground equipment and structures; Playground surfacing systems; Hard-surface and multi-use play courts; Outdoor recreational and athletic surfaces; and, Perimeter features, furnishings, and appurtenances. The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, tools, equipment, materials, transportation, documentation, and incidentals necessary to ensure playgrounds remain safe, serviceable, compliant, and operational throughout the period of performance.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. title: USHMM-RFI-2027-MSSP
description: DISCLAIMER / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE:This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by USHMM to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) is conducting formal market research to evaluate commercial vendor capabilities, industry pricing benchmarks, federal/commercial labor rates, and available contract acquisition vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS SIN 54151HACS, NASA SEWP, CIO-SP3/4, SAM.gov) for re-procuring comprehensive Managed Information Technology (IT) Security, Multi-Cloud/DevSecOps Architecture, Network Engineering, and specialized Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) operational activities. The primary objective of this market research effort is to evaluate whether competitive commercial marketplace capabilities exist to: Sustain, support, and execute day-to-day operations across USHMM's existing "As-Is" securityinfrastructure without operational disruption or increased organizational risk. Perform rigorous security architecture evaluations, threat modeling, gap analyses, and complianceassessments against industry-best security and privacy standards (NIST SP 800-53 r5, FISMA, PCI DSSv4.2.1, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, CSF 2.0). Architect and recommend a modernized, cost-effective "To-Be" security state incorporating ZeroTrust architecture, automated orchestration, tool consolidation, and a Government OwnedContractor Operated (GOCO) Security Operations Center (SOC) framework. Execute a seamless, structured transition lifecycle from the "As-Is" state to the "To-Be" operationalmodel within strict schedule and budget parameters. Pricing Benchmarks & Market Rate Expectations Provide feedback on the commercial feasibility of managing this scope under a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)monthly fee structure. Provide fully burdened hourly commercial labor rates or GSA schedule rates in the Washington, DCMetropolitan Area for equivalent labor categories (CISO, Security Architect, DevSecOps Engineer,Security Analyst, Network/System Engineer). Submission Instructions & Response Format Response Deadline: All responses shall be submitted electronically no later than October 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submission Format: Responses must be submitted in PDF or Microsoft Word format, strictly limited to no more than fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and labor rate tables). Point of Contact: Submissions and any clarifying technical inquiries must be emailed to Mary Green, USHMM Contracting Officer at magreen@ushmm.org with the subject line "RFI Response - USHMM Managed IT Security & MSSP Services".

title: Request for Information on Combat Boot Sock
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the U.S. Marine Corps Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) to identify potential sources to provide a Combat Boot Sock. The goal is to provide warfighting capability and mission support in various environments by enhancing foot comfort, durability, and performance for military personnel. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and harvey.walker1@usmc.mil by October 30, 2026 by 5 PM EST. Background: Program Manager Combat Support Systems (PM CSS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing a high-performance combat boot sock that meets the requirements of Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003. The sock is intended for use with the applicable standard-issue combat boots identified in the purchase description. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market-research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to procure any product or service. Description: The Marine Corps is seeking sources capable of manufacturing a durable, reliable combat boot sock designed to provide comfort, protection, and performance during demanding operational use. The sock shall meet the following Salient Characteristics specified in Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003, including, but not limited to, the following key requirements: Sock shall feature an over-the-calf length with cushioning comfort to protect the wearer from hot spots, pressure points, and blisters when wearing combat boots, and they provide graduated compression to promote blood flow from the foot with a non-slip top cuff opening. The foot of each sock includes contouring for the sock to stay in place without bunching, arch support, a gore heel and toe for improved fit, and nylon reinforcement at the heel and toe for durability. A seamless toe closure or a recessed closure with equivalent low profile is used for comfort and durability. Basic Materials. The sock shall contain wool a minimum of 52% wool (no coarser than US 60s (25 microns or finer)), a minimum of 20% nylon, and a minimum of 1% spandex and shall not contain cotton or rayon fiber. Shade. Shall be in accordance with section 3.3 of the Purchase Description Visual shade matching. Shall be in accordance with section 3.4 of the Purchase Description The finished socks shall conform to the requirements specified in table II when tested as specified. **Please refer to Table II. Sock performance requirement** Deliverables: This is a Sources Sought Announcement / RFI to identify potential sources. Based on responses, the Government may plan for a future acquisition. Interested parties should demonstrate their capability to produce socks meeting the above requirements. The Government may request samples for future evaluation. Submission Instructions: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. Responses are for information and planning purposes only. This Sources Sought Announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Marine Corps has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending responses regarding this requirement to PAE MC via e-mail ONLY to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 30, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. If you hold a GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, please identify your contract number. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 26, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement.

description: UPDATE (23 September 2026): Due to the significant number of questions received, this Special Notice is amended to extend the Request for Information (RFI) submission deadline. Accordingly, the PPA invites industry partners and service providers to submit detailed information regarding integration costs, associated software development timelines, standard industry practices, and recommendations for testing and risk mitigation when connecting their internal software systems to a central Government platform. description: This notice is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is issued by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for information and planning purposes, pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, Market Research. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Participants are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs that result from responding to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Pursuant to Executive Order (EO) 14271, Ensuring Commercial Cost-Effective Solutions in Federal Contracts, the Chief Procurement Officer is committed to purchasing commercial items and performing robust market research to identify commercial products and services that meet the Government�s needs. description: Предметът на обществената поръчка включва изработка и доставка на холограмни стикери по обособени позиции, в частта по Обособена позиция 2 „Изработка и доставка на комплект „Знак и стикер за първоначален технически преглед на МПС“ - 2 000 000 бр. холографски стикера и 2 000 000 бр. знак със съответните холограмни реквизити. ​На основание чл. 21, ал. 6 от ЗОП, във връзка с чл. 7 от ППЗОП, обособена позиция № 1 с предмет: „Изработка и доставка на холограмни стикери за служебните карти на служителите на МВР" - 60 000 бр., ще се възлага чрез директно възлагане, по реда на чл. 21​, ал. 6 от ЗОП, съобразно прогнозната й стойност от 75 180,00 евро без ДДС. Стойността на обособена позиция № 1 не надхвърля стойността от 79 998,77 евро без ДДС и 20 на сто от общата прогнозна стойност на поръчката, която е 5 995 180,00 евро без ДДС. Съгласно разпоредба на чл. 7, ал. 1 от ППЗОП, остатъчната стойност на поръчката е 5 920 000,00 евро без ДДС. В изпълнение на чл. 21, ал. 6 от ЗОП, независимо от размера на остатъчната стойност на поръчката, тя се възлага по реда, приложим към общата прогнозна стойност на цялата поръчка. ​​​​​​​В настоящата обществена поръчка оферта се подава САМО по обособена позиция № 2 „Изработка и доставка на комплект „Знак и стикер за първоначален технически преглед на МПС“. ​​​​​​​Обособена позиция № 1 ще се възлага по реда на чл. 21, ал. 6 от ЗОП.

title: France – Processing and clearing services – Fourniture de chèques emploi service universels (CESU), dématérialisés ou non, aux agents des ministères sociaux.
description: Dans le cadre de la politique conduite pour favoriser les services à la personne – Plan de développement des services à la personne LOI N° 2005-841 du 26 juillet 2005, les ministères sociaux ont mis en place, depuis septembre 2006 le chèque emploi service universel (CESU) préfinancé pour une partie de leurs agents, destinés notamment au paiement : • Du salaire net d'un salarié employé directement dans le cadre des services à la personne ; • De prestations de services à la personne fournies par des organismes agréés ; • Des structures d'accueil de jeunes enfants (crèches, garderies, centres de loisirs…) ; • De structures agréées, habilitées à effectuer, pour le compte de particuliers employeurs, l'ensemble des formalités liées à l'emploi d'un salarié à domicile (recrutement, gestion administrative du salarié, ...) ; • De prestations d'aide à domicile délivrées à ses ascendants par des salariés employés à domicile ou des organismes agréés, si ces ascendants sont bénéficiaires de l'allocation personnalisée d'autonomie (APA). Le CESU est un titre de paiement nominatif à montant prédéfini délivré par les ministères sociaux qui en assurent le financement intégral.

description: Tämän dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (DPS) kohteena on IT kehittämisen ja ylläpidon palvelut Turun kaupungin asiakkaille. title: (b26065-1) Assainissement et optimisation de la salle du Jubilé de Macolin / CFC 421
description:
La salle du jubilé a été conçue par l'architecte biennois Max Schlup et est classée comme objet digne de protection dans l'inventaire du service cantonal des monuments historiques. C'est un bien culturel d'importance nationale. La salle du jubilé est un témoin important de la culture architecturale des années 80 et un représentant majeur de la culture architecturale programmatique de l'architecture du pied du Jura.

La salle de sport est le centre national de performance des cadres suisses de la gymnastique artistique et des gymnastes.

Après quatre décennies d'utilisation, différents éléments sont arrivés à la fin de leur cycle de vie et doivent être rénovés pour un fonctionnement sans faille. De plus, les exigences des utilisateurs envers le gymnase ont évolué au fil du temps.

Le projet comprend la rénovation de l'enveloppe du bâtiment et des surfaces intérieures, le remplacement de l'ensemble des installations techniques et de l'éclairage ainsi que diverses adaptations aux normes et standards actuels. Avec des modifications du plan, les zones de vestiaires seront réorganisées, des salles de réunion couplables et une salle de musculation seront créées, ainsi que des bureaux pour les entraîneurs et une salle de théorie seront réorganisés. En outre, la salle de sport sera réorganisée avec la construction de fosses supplémentaires et d'autres adaptations.

Les travaux ne sont pas effectués en cours d'utilisation.

  • Arbeiten im Bereich von Kantonsstrassen und Bahnanlagen mit erhöhten Anforderungen an Sicherheit, Bauablauf und Koordination.

title: Udbud vedrørende anskaffelse af mobilt opdæmningsmateriel
description: Udbud vedrørende anskaffelse af mobilt opdæmningsmateriel Beskrivelse (dansk): Beredskabsstyrelsen ("BRS") ønsker sammen med landets 30 kommunale redningsberedskaber ("de Kommunale Beredskaber") at indgå en rammeaftale om anskaffelse af mobilt dæmningsmateriel i form af fritstående oversvømmelsesbarrierer. Anskaffelsen har primært til formål at understøtte BRS' og de Kommunale Beredskabers akutte håndtering af klimahændelser, herunder ved varsling om forhøjet vandstand fra bagland såvel som havvand, samt ved indsats i forbindelse med større brande. Det mobile dæmningsmateriel skal anvendes både selvstændigt i forbindelse med håndteringen af bl.a. klimahændelser, ligesom det skal indgå som supplement til BRS' og de Kommunale Beredskabers eksisterende opdæmningsmateriel. Materiellet skal kunne anvendes i flere forskellige indsatsscenarier. Det skal for det første kunne etableres hurtigt og fleksibelt over varierende strækninger ved ekstraordinære vandstandsstigninger, herunder ved akut indsats i baglandet, f.eks. ved søer og åer, samt ved kyster og havne. Det skal for det andet kunne benyttes til beskyttelse af enkeltobjekter, f.eks. kritisk infrastruktur. Det skal for det tredje kunne anvendes som vandreservoir i forbindelse med større brandindsatser, hvor vand anbringes i reservoiret, hvorfra én eller flere pumper fordeler vandet til indsatsområdet. Det mobile dæmningsmateriel skal have en primær højde svarende til højden på BRS' eksisterende og mest anvendte opdæmningsmateriel. Da de lokale beredskabers risikovurderinger og behov varierer, ønskes der herudover tilbudt opdæmningsmateriel i andre højder, som muliggør tilpasning til områder med behov for lavere eller højere opdæmning. Det er væsentligt, at materiellet tillader hurtig, let og effektiv transport, etablering og nedtagning, herunder at håndteringen kan ske med et minimum af ressourcer og på en arbejdsmiljømæssigt forsvarlig måde. Materiellet forudsættes at kunne benyttes flere gange. Materiellet vil blive oplagret på lager og transporteret til indsatsområderne via lastbil. Under indsættelse skal materiellet kunne håndteres ved håndkraft, herunder aflæsses, opsættes, nedtages og læsses, af et minimalt mandskab. Rammeaftalen har en varighed af 4 år fra underskrift.

title: Sweden – Construction work – Nya Vård- och omsorgsplatser Eldslösa
description: Projektet Mjölby kommun har för avsikt att uppföra ett nytt vård- och omsorgsboende på Eldslösa omfattande 80 platser inklusive korttidsplatser, och är avsett för äldre personer med behov av vård och omsorg dygnet runt. Byggnaden planeras i två våningar med totalt åtta avdelningar, där varje avdelning omfattar ca 10 lägenheter med tillhörande gemensamma utrymmen. Boendet utformas med fokus på hög tillgänglighet, trygghet, hemlik miljö och god arbetsmiljö. Varje lägenhet ska vara fullvärdig och innehålla eget hygienrum, pentry samt vara anpassad för vård och lyft. Gemensamma funktioner omfattar bland annat vardagsrum, matsal och avdelningskök, samt tillgång till balkonger eller uteplatser. Utöver boendedelarna innehåller byggnaden gemensamma publika funktioner såsom huvudentré med lobby, samlingssal/konferens, träningskök, gym, besökstoaletter samt ett tillagningskök dimensionerat för ca 100 portioner. Det planeras även omfattande personalutrymmen, administrativa lokaler, expeditioner för sjuksköterskor och terapeuter samt erforderliga drift- och teknikytor. Utemiljön är en central del av projektet och ska utformas som en tillgänglig, trygg och stimulerande trädgårdsmiljö, med möjlighet till utevistelse året runt. Den innehåller bland annat uteplatser, inglasat uterum, gångstråk, odlingsytor samt vara delvis inhängnad för att skapa trygghet för de boende. För att säkerställa byggnadens robusthet planeras funktioner för nödvattenförsörjning, krislager och reservkraft. Reservkraftsanläggningen placeras i en fristående byggnad inom fastigheten. Byggnaden ska projekteras för Miljöbyggnad 4.0 för endast indikatorn energi. Indikatorn energi ska klara silvernivå. Övriga indikatorer är ej aktuella. Ny detaljplan har vunnit laga kraft och beställaren förbereder nu bygglovsprocess. Ytor Huvudbyggnad Hus A ca 8300 m2 BTA (inkl vind), 3900 m2 BYA Hus B ca 110 m2 BTA Tomtens area: ca 16 000 m2 UMA Förutsättningar för projektet Projektet handlas upp som generalentreprenad på entreprenadformen totalentreprenad, ABT 06. Beställaren har valt att genomföra Entreprenaden med utökad samverkan – s k strategisk partnering - som närmare beskrivs i entreprenadkontraktet. Beställaren har projekterat fram ett förfrågningsunderlag som vidare kommer att förfinas tillsammans med entreprenören. De tekniska handlingarna presenteras under ”Övriga handlingar” enligt ABT 06 kap 1 § 3 pkt 7. Entreprenaden kommer att utföras med iakttagande av en fasindelning med planering och projektering (Fas 1) å ena sidan och detaljprojektering och utförande (Fas 2) å andra sidan, som beskrivs närmare i entreprenadkontraktet. Avsikten med upphandlingsformen är att med samlad kompetens och kreativitet åstadkomma ett funktionellt, kvalitativt och hållbart projekt. Projektet genomförs i öppen samverkan mellan parterna med ABT 06 som grund. Arbetsprocess Entreprenören ska i denna upphandling lämna anbud på entreprenörsarvode och ett fast pris för tjänstemannakostnad under fas 2. Offererade priser ska vidare vara gällande under arbetsprocessens fas 1 och fas 2. Se 07.2 Anbudsutvärderingsmodell. Under fas 1 ska entreprenören i samråd med beställaren upprätta ett anbud (kalkyl) som underlag för en vidare kontraktsförhandling mellan parterna avseende projektering av bygghandlingar och förestående produktionsarbeten. Kontraktet möjliggör således fas 2 som avser projektering av bygghandlingar och förestående produktionsarbeten. Fas 2 tecknas som en option där Beställaren har ensidig rätt att göra avrop på fas 2. I det fall entreprenören och beställaren inte kommit överens under fas 1 har beställaren äganderätt på samtliga framtagna handlingar under fas 1 samt förfoganderätt att utföra separat upphandling på projektet. Se vidare i entreprenadkontrakt.

A permit or permits to provide high-quality public service in the operation and maintenance of Government-owned recreation facilities located on the Powder River, Medicine Wheel, and Tongue Ranger Districts, Bighorn National Forest, will be issued. The permit or permits will include 31 campgrounds and 2 picnic grounds. A facility tour led by the Forest is scheduled for September 25 and 26, 2026. Interested parties must RSVP to Andrea Maichak at andrea.maichak@usda.gov by Friday, September 18, 2026. All applications must be received by close of business (4:30 p.m.) on Friday, October 30, 2026.

description: RED INTERNACIONAL B-LIVE, es la entidad única organizadora del Encuentro Internacional de Fotoperiodismo de Asturias, según se indica en la página Web del encuentro: https://fotoperiodismoasturias.org/. Según consta en el informe propuesta del contrato el patrocinio publicitario del Encuentro Internacional de Fotoperiodismo de Asturias es una plataforma idónea para reforzar el posicionamiento de la marca “Asturias Paraíso Natural”, proyectando la imagen de la región como un destino cultural, creativo, sostenible y abierto al conocimiento, a través de una programación con capacidad de atracción turística y una importante repercusión en medios de comunicación, redes sociales y circuitos culturales nacionales e internacionales. Estas características hacen que esta colaboración sea única y que no exista una alternativa o sustituto razonable y que la ausencia de competencia no es consecuencia de una configuración restrictiva de los requisitos y criterios para adjudicar el contrato.

description: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.305, the U.S. Army Contracting Command � Rock Island at Picatinny (ACC-RI-PICA), on behalf of the Project Manager for Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), is hereby posting the Justification and Approval (J&A) for a sole-source action to the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs (DEMA). This justification, Control Number CAO-26-0032, provides the authority for a one-year extension of services under contract W15QKN-21-C-0002 for the continued storage, material handling, maintenance, and inspection of 155mm artillery ammunition at Camp Navajo, AZ. This action is necessary to ensure continuity of these critical services and prevent a gap in mission support while a long-term follow-on contract is finalized. The action was justified in accordance with FAR 13.501(a)(1)(ii), as DEMA is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Government's requirements without unacceptable schedule delays and duplication of cost. description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE W912HV27RA001 ARMY AIR DEFENSE ARTILLERY VEHICLE MAINTENANCE SHOP KADENA AIR BASE, OKINAWA, JAPAN Introduction: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan District (POJ), Okinawa Area Office (OAO) is providing a Pre-Solicitation notice pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 5.101(a) for an upcoming Request for Proposal (RFP). This notice is not a solicitation. *SITE VISIT: (a) An organized site visit has been scheduled: (i) 19 October 2026 at 9:30 a.m. Japan Standard Time (JST) (ii) Location: Meet at building 4040 on Kadena Air Base, Okinawa, Japan (see attached map). The attendee no later than 1 October 2026 at 12:00 pm, JST list shall include full name, company name, email address, phone number, and whether temporary base access is required (see section (b)) below if temporary base access is required). (iv) Vehicle Information: Make, Model, Color, and License plate (for rental cars write "Rental car") (v) If there is a change in a POC list after 1 October 2026, please provide that as soon as possible. Primary POC: Terry Schlautman, Project Manager Telephone: 081-98-970-9269 Email: Terry.P.Schlautman@usace.army.mil Alternate POC: Jihye Park Telephone: 098-970-9391 Email: jihye.park@usace.army.mil (b) Participants requiring base escort to Kadena Air Base Submit the names of all attendees via email to the POC above no later than 1 October 2026 at 12:00 PM, JST. List shall include full name of person, company name, email address, Phone number, citizenship, gender, country of birth, date of birth, and ID number. This information must be provided in advance to ensure access to the military base. If there is a change in a POC list after October 2026, please provide that as soon as possible. (i) Acceptable ID number for Japanese citizens are Passport, My Number, or Driver�s license. Acceptable ID number for Non-Japanese citizens are Passport with valid landing permission or Japan Residence Card. US citizens must additionally provide their Social Security Number. Please provide a scanned copy of the ID being used. (ii) Attendees requiring a base escort shall meet at 9:00 JST at the Gate 1 Visitor Control Center. Required documentation for base escort on the day: Valid Picture Identification (ID). Valid IDs are required for entry onto all Military Installations in Okinawa, Japan. Driver's License, Passport or My Number Card (with photograph) are considered valid picture IDs. Once a base pass is issued, USACE personnel will escort attendees directly to the site. All attendees are expected to exit the base immediately following the site (iii) For registration after 1 October 2026, contact the POCs. PROJECT INFORMATION: Project Title: Army Air Defense Artillery (ADA) Vehicle Maintenance Shop (VMS), Kadena Air Base Project Location: Okinawa, Japan Product Service Code (PSC): Y1AZ � Construction of Other Administration Facilities and Service Buildings NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Estimated Project Magnitude: Between �15,000,000,000 and �30,000,000,000 Construction Type: Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Construction Period of Performance: 1,260 calendar days Projected Solicitation Issue: October 2026 Projected Proposal Due Date: February 2027 Anticipated Contract Award: September 2027 Project Description: This project will provide a VMS (36,000 square feet) and associated facilities. The work includes demolition of existing structures. The primary facilities include the VMS, unit supply storage building, special foundations, organizational storage building, petroleum, oil and lubricant (POL) and hazardous waste storage buildings, wash platform, organizational vehicle parking, supply support storage shed, water storage tank, swing space, cybersecurity and antiterrorism/force protection (AT/FP) measures, building information systems, fire protection and alarm systems, intrusion detection system (IDS) installation, and energy monitoring control systems (EMCS) connection. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, storm drainage, paving, parking, walkways, lighting, information systems, landscaping and signage. Heating and air conditioning will be provided by a self-contained system. The project involves significant earthwork and sequential construction project management. SOLICITATION INFORMATION: The Government anticipates an issuance of the RFP utilizing the Best Value Trade Off (BVTO) Source Selection as described in RFO 15.103-1. Please see the attached draft Section 00 22 00 Instructions to Offerors Supplement (Evaluation Criteria), Drawings, and Specifications for further information. Documents are likely to change; reference only the final solicitation with attachments, drawings and specifications once they are issued in PIEE. All interested companies shall be actively registered in the SAM database in order to be eligible for award of Government contracts. Information on registration and annual confirmation requirements may be found at http://www.sam.gov. For a Joint Venture, the Joint Venture as an independent entity must be registered in SAM as such. All solicitation documents, drawings, and specifications will be posted on the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) with notice on System for Award Management (SAM) when issued. Interested vendors are responsible for monitoring PIEE/SAM websites for issuance of the solicitation and/or amendments. It is recommended that contractors create their PIEE Solicitation Module account as soon as possible and not wait for the proposal due date, as access may take time. Instructions for registration can be found through: https://piee.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/web/homepage/vendorGettingStartedHelp.xhtml Step 2: Upload offer in the Solicitation Module through https://piee.eb.mil/ . Instructions for uploading an offer can be found through: https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/sol/documents/Proposal_Manager_Functions.pdf Firms which have not done business with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan Engineering District, are requested to visit the following website: https://www.poj.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/ for general information. Specifically, a prospective offeror must be duly authorized to operate and conduct construction business in Japan and must fully comply with all applicable laws, decrees, labor standards, and regulations of Japan during the performance of the resulting contracts. In addition, offerors must possess a Japanese civil construction (doboku isshiki koji) license or Japanese architectural construction (kenchiku isshiki koji) license by the proposal due date and time. title: EQUIPMENT SUPPORT SERVICES (ESS) GUAM
description: The Naval Facilities (NAVFAC) Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (EXWC), Port Hueneme, California has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) under solicitation number N3943026R0009 or a Firm Fixed Price, Single Award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ). NAVFAC EXWC has a requirement to support an Equipment Support Services (ESS) Contract that includes an Equipment Maintenance, Repair with Corrosion Prevention and Control (abatement and repair) program. Some of the services include operational repairs, maintenance (preventative and corrective) services, corrective repairs, washing, spot painting, corrosion prevention and repair for all Civil Engineering Support Equipment (CESE), Civil Engineer End Items (CEEI), Material Handling Equipment (MHE), Weight Handling Equipment (WHE), support vehicles, and Containerized Base Camp Facility items located at Naval Base Guam, Guam (NBG), or various locations off NBG, but still on the island of Guam. The closing time and date for receipt of proposals is 5:00PM PT on 30 October 2026 as indicated on the solicitation. This acquisition will be solicited as 100 percent small business set-aside. The Government will only accept offers from small business concerns. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates the award of an IDIQ with base ordering period of sixty (60) months, and a 6 month option period for extension of services. Individual task orders under this contract will be firm fixed price (FFP). At the time of award, the Government will issue a minimum guarantee as the first task order. The estimated award date is February 2027. The maximum value of all task orders placed under this contract will not exceed $17,000,000.00. The solicitation and attachments are available to view and/or download online via the Solicitation Module in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil, which can be accessed through the links included solicitation notice N3943026R0009. This will be the only method of distribution; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the solicitation module in PIEE periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. Offerors must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov in order to receive an award under this procurement. All questions concerning this solicitation are due by 12:00PM PT on 09 October 2026 and must be addressed to Jake O. Blas via email at jake.o.blas.civ@us.navy.mil and secondary POC, Desiree Garcia at desiree.e.garcia9.civ@us.navy.mil.

description: Title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract Type: Pre-Solicitation Notice Location: Primarily at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Pacific. Solicitation Method: NAVFAC intends to issue one (1) solicitation in September 2026 that results in the award of approximately five (5) Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC) primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock. Solicitation and award of the MACC is anticipated to utilize single phase (one-step) Design-Build (DB) selection procedures. Anticipated Evaluation Factors: Anticipated non-cost/price and price evaluation factors for the solicitation are summarized as follows: Factor 1 � Technical Approach (acceptable/unacceptable) Factor 2 � Experience Factor 3 � Past Performance Factor 4 � Small Business Utilization and Participation Factor 5 � Safety (acceptable/unacceptable) Factor 6 � Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC) Management Plan Price NOTE: The Government anticipates that evaluation of Factor 2 � Experience will encompass relevant projects for BOTH construction projects AND design projects. Period of Performance/Maximum Value: The period of performance is anticipated to be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. NAICS Codes: This MACC will encompass a wide range of DB and Design-Bid-Build (DBB) type projects primarily representative of North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) codes 237990 (primary) Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction as well as 236220 (secondary) Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Task Order Range: The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. For evaluation purposes, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that construction projects with a minimum value of $350,000,000 will be deemed relevant. The Navy anticipates that most work under the MACC will be initiated by task order(s) that are competed amongst all the MACC holders (firms awarded one of the potential contracts). Additionally, all MACC holders may be issued task orders for the same scope of work for ECI and/or ATC or where justified, task order awards may be issued to a single MACC holder. The Navy makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, each MACC holder is anticipated to receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. As subsequent task orders are awarded which exceed the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee, the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee will be de-obligated and the Government�s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Bonding Capacity: To qualify for this MACC, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that Offerors will need to demonstrate single project bonding capacity of $1,000,000,000 and an aggregate bonding capacity of $3,000,000,000. Acquisition Timeline (Anticipated): Industry Day: 20 August 2026 (actual) Issue MACC Solicitation: 30 September 2026 MACC Pre-Proposal Conference: October 2026 MACC Proposals Due: December 2026 MACC Award: June 2027 Issue Alternative Technical Concept (ATC) Task Order(s): June 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Initial): August 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Final): November 2027 RFP Task Order Marine Package #1: November-December 2027 Planned task order award of Marine Package #1: June 2028 Purpose and Scope: The focus of this MACC will be the construction of a new proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock in support of SIOP requirements at PSNS & IMF, located at NBK Bremerton, Washington. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock preferred location is within the existing Dry Dock 3 footprint, existing Pier 6, and existing Pier 7; and will include dry dock drainage, dewatering, and flooding systems; a caisson; roadways and rail networks; portal crane track; access and egress elements; mechanical, electrical, and communications systems; support buildings; and utility routing tunnels. The proposed project also includes demolition of facilities and utilities. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock is a fully pressure-relieved dry dock capable of accommodating shipyard repair services for the newest Ford-class aircraft carrier, Nimitz-class carriers, and other surface and subsurface ships served by PSNS & IMF. Dredging south of Multi-Mission Dry Dock is proposed for the Double-Wall Cofferdams, which provides means to support construction of Multi-Mission Dry Dock in the dry, and provides hydraulic cutoff in the permanent condition. The bathymetry in Sinclair Inlet provides adequate water depths to support the drafts of the respective design vessels at berth and during docking/undocking evolutions. Site access is anticipated to be a combination of a temporary fixed pier southeast of existing Building 460, a contractor access road at Bremerton Gate, existing Piers 6 & 7, Dry Dock 3, and the South Gate vehicle inspection building. Prior to establishing the above-described entry points the Navy requires the contractor to install a temporary Controlled Industrial Area (CIA) fence that will encompass the project site. For more information on the proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock project see: https://bremertonwaterfrontimprovementseis.com/ https://multimissiondrydock.com/ Potential Risk Mitigations: The Navy is considering the following risk mitigation measures including but not limited to: Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) Award Fee and/or Schedule Incentive Reduced small business subcontracting targets One or more of the items under this acquisition may be subject to Free Trade Agreements or the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement.
